newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end up as TEM rates seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end up as TEM rates seen falling.

text.p: Caracas stocks edged ahead in light trade, boosted by an expected fall in TEM yields but constrained by a local liquidity squeeze and investor caution ahead of news from the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting, traders said.
Market bellwether Electricidad de Caracas led trade, rising 0.28 percent to close at 518.75 bolivars after falling as low as 517.31 from Monday's 538.00 close on a one for 25 stock dividend.
"Electricidad's adjustment dampened the market to start with," Profimerca broker Miguel Gonzalez said.

"But when the tiny TEM auction size was announced and the market saw interest rates falling, the bolsa picked up some steam," he added. The bourse's 19-share index rose 0.25 percent to close at 6,564.93 points as among traded issues, 11 rose, 14 fell and 12 finished flat.
Merinvest's composite, which includes telephone company CANTV, meanwhile gained 0.14 percent to end at 104.03.
Trade volume was a low 32 million shares, worth 7.5 billion bolivars ($15.6 million) as investors scrambled for bolivars after the overnight lending rate soared to 90 percent Monday.
With bolivar supply still tight after many investors have bought dollars in recent days, brokers were divided as to whether Wednesday's auction of 30 billion bolivars of TEMs would see rates rise.
The Caracas bolsa's session closed before the announcement that the U.S. Fed decided not to raise interest rates.
